title: Post-incident clarity note: verified data integrity and next steps
content:
TL;DR
On 2028-12-17 between 09:12 and 11:37 UTC a subset of customer traffic was routed to an unintended model variant during an automated rollout. The variant delivered lower relevance scores for semantic-search style requests and produced higher token usage (on average +28% tokens per request). We have verified there was no customer data loss and no unauthorized access. This note explains what happened, who was affected, what we fixed, and recommended customer actions.

Scope and customer impact
- Impact window: 2028-12-17 09:12 → 2028-12-17 11:37 UTC (observed across eu-west and us-central regions).
- Symptoms observed: degraded search relevance for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, elevated token counts per session, and a modest increase in 5xx error rate for streaming sessions (0.6% -> 1.9%).
- Affected customers: ~4.7% of active tenants had a portion of their requests served by the mismatched variant. For the majority of those tenants the issue was partial (10–60% of requests affected) and limited to inference calls routed through model-route aliases configured with automatic rollout.
- Data integrity: We verified request/response logs and KV caches for affected requests; no customer data was lost, truncated, or exfiltrated. All persisted artifacts (logs, embeddings, user-provided context) remain intact.

Root cause (summary)
- During an automated canary rollout, a routing policy regression in the smart-router service matched requests at an alias-level that did not include the new quantization-compatibility tag required by the runtime kernels. This allowed a quantized-optimized variant (128Q) to receive traffic intended for the full-precision relevance model (FP32-rlv).
- The quantized variant uses a compression pathway that changes tokenization alignment for certain prompt patterns used in RAG templates. Combined with a slightly different ranking head calibration, relevance scores dropped and tokenized length increased for many inputs.
- The regression was introduced in runtime routing rules by PR #2431, which interacted with the rollout orchestrator's alias-matching heuristics. The PR passed unit tests but missed an integration scenario for alias-tag precedence.

Mitigations enacted (what we did immediately)
1) At 09:23 UTC we detected unusual signal in the relevance SLO dashboard (drop in top-1 recall for synchronized eval set). On-call engineer triaged and temporarily halted the ongoing rollout.
2) At 09:45 UTC we applied a targeted routing override to pin all traffic for the affected aliases to the FP32-rlv variant while we investigated.
3) We rolled back PR #2431 in the routing service at 10:12 UTC to eliminate the alias-precedence regression and re-ran the orchestration dry-run.
4) At 10:58 UTC traffic was confirmed to have returned to expected model variants and metrics started trending back to baseline; full normalization by 11:37 UTC.
5) We ran a verification sweep against a canonical suite of RAG prompts and customer-provided samples (when customers opted in) to ensure model outputs and tokenization alignment were restored.

Permanent fixes (in-progress / planned)
- Short term (next 2 weeks): enforce alias-tag precedence unit and integration tests in the routing repo; add a blocking gate in rollout orchestrator that checks quantization-compatibility tags match target alias definitions before any traffic shift.
- Medium term (1–2 months): expand rollout dry-run coverage to include representative RAG prompt templates and synthetic tokenization mismatch detectors; add end-to-end canary traffic simulation for at least one production workload per region.
- Long term (3–6 months): introduce an automated telemetry alert that correlates sudden per-request token-increase with model-variant changes and triggers automated pause + rollback of rollouts.

Customer-facing remediation and offers
- All affected tenants will receive a detailed per-tenant event summary with sample request IDs and the percent of requests affected (we will not share raw user content).
- For customers who experienced billing impact due to increased token charges during the window, Redwood will issue a credit equal to the incremental token-cost incurred during the incident window. We will calculate credits automatically and post a line-item to billing statements within 7 business days.
- For customers who request it, we will run a one-off verification pass of their most critical prompt/route pairs against current model variants and provide suggested pinning or alias configurations to prevent similar exposure.

Recommended customer actions (if you want additional protection)
- Pin critical routes to explicit model IDs instead of alias-level automatic rollouts if deterministic output and cost predictability are required.
- For RAG or search-like workloads, add a short integration test that validates top-k recall on a small set of representative prompts after any model change. We can help run this test via a professional-services engagement.
- Enable the optional ‘quantization-compatibility’ tag on routes where you rely on strict tokenization alignment; our runtime will reject mismatched variants when this tag is enforced.

FAQ (quick answers)
Q: Was any PII exposed or deleted?
A: No. We verified there was no unauthorized access and no deletion of persisted customer data. Logs show normal authentication and no abnormal data exports.

Q: Why did token counts increase?
A: The quantized variant’s tokenization and compression pathway produced different token boundaries for a subset of prompts, increasing tokenized length for those inputs. That is a side-effect of the specific quantization and token alignment heuristics in that variant.

Q: Will you change how rollouts are performed?
A: Yes — we are adding blocking checks and additional integration tests to the rollout pipeline to prevent mismatch scenarios. Rolling changes will remain gradual, but with stricter compatibility gating.

Next steps for us (customer success & engineering)
- Customer-success: prepare per-tenant summaries and coordinate credits with billing. Drafts will be sent to named account contacts by 2028-12-22.
- Engineering: merge routing-tests PR and deploy the gating check to staging by 2028-12-24; deploy to production after a 48-hour soak in staging.
- Product: review default alias semantics and consider introducing a more explicit naming convention for quantization-aware variants in the model catalog.

If you have specific customers you want priority outreach for, or you have samples you want us to run through the verification sweep, add them to the linked doc (Confluence CONF-4283) or reply to this note.

Prepared by: Customer Success (Evelyn Chen) with Engineering (Marco Ruiz, Tom Becker).
Document history: draft created 2028-12-18; updated with remediation details 2028-12-20.
